subject: Chemistry
name: Theory (Core)
description: Core theory covering structure and bonding, Earth and Moon composition and iron extraction, fuels and energy, halogens, air and fertilisers, acids bases and salts, organic chemistry, and metals and electroplating.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Structures of seven substances A–G: A (CH₄), B (PCl₃), C (N₂ triple bond), D (CO₂), E (H₂O bent), F (C₂H₄ ethene alkene), G (C₄H₁₀ alkane). State which structure represents a compound that contains atoms of a Group VII element.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: State which structure represents an element with a giant covalent structure.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: State which structure represents a compound that turns anhydrous copper(II) sulfate blue.

parts.label: a(iv)
parts.question: State which structure represents an element that conducts electricity. (Note: none of these are metallic; the answer is the giant covalent element C which can conduct in some forms; or interpret as none being metallic conductors.)

parts.label: a(v)
parts.question: State which structure represents an unsaturated hydrocarbon.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Describe a test for an unsaturated hydrocarbon.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Name the two products formed when compound A (CH₄, methane) undergoes complete combustion.

parts.question: Table compares element percentages by mass in Earth's crust vs Moon's crust. Earth: O 46.60, Si 29.50, Al 8.20, Fe 5.00, Ca 3.60, Mg 2.00, Ti 0.55, other 4.55. Moon: O 40.00, Si 19.50, Fe 13.50, Al 7.50, Ca 7.50, Mg 5.50, Ti 3.00. Deduce the percentage by mass of the other elements in the Moon's crust.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: State which element is present in the Earth's crust in the greatest percentage by mass.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: Give two major differences in the composition of the Earth's crust and the Moon's crust.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Complete the diagram to show the electron arrangement in a silicon atom (atomic number 14). Draw shells with electrons: 2,8,4.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Iron reacts with oxygen to form Fe₃O₄. Complete the chemical equation: .....Fe + .....O₂ → Fe₃O₄

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Complete these sentences about iron extraction in a blast furnace using words from the list: air, decomposed, dioxide, hydrogen, iron, monoxide, oxidised, reduced, slag. The raw materials are iron ore, limestone and ............ . Carbon monoxide reacts with iron(III) oxide to produce iron. In this reaction iron(III) oxide is ............ . Limestone decomposes to produce calcium oxide and carbon ............ . Calcium oxide reacts with impurities in the iron ore to form ............ .

blanks.prompt: raw materials: iron ore, limestone and __________
calcium oxide reacts with impurities to form __________

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Iron is converted to steel using oxygen. Explain how the oxygen removes the carbon.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Choose from the list the name of the other type of compound used to convert iron into steel: acidic oxide, alcohol, basic oxide, hydrocarbon.

parts.label: d(iii)
parts.question: Steel is an alloy. Choose the diagram J, K, L or M which best represents an alloy (different sized atoms mixed in a lattice).

parts.label: a
parts.question: Chemical reactions can be endothermic or exothermic. State the meaning of the term endothermic.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Diagram shows apparatus to compare energy released when 100 cm³ of water is heated by burning different liquid fuels P, Q, R, S. Results: P (3g burned, +6°C), Q (2g burned, +8°C), R (1g burned, +3°C), S (3g burned, +9°C). Deduce which fuel releases the least energy per gram.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Name a gas that is used as a fuel.

parts.label: d
parts.question: An energy level diagram (energy vs progress of reaction) shows a downward slope from left to right. Complete the diagram by writing reactants on the left (higher energy) and products on the right (lower energy).

parts.question: The radioactive isotope ²³⁵U is used as a source of energy. State one other use of radioactive isotopes.

parts.question: Table shows halogen properties: Cl (mp –101°C, bp –35°C, density 0.003), Br (mp –7°C, bp 59°C, density 3.12), I (mp 114°C, bp 184°C), At (bp 302°C, density 6.35). Predict the density of iodine and the boiling point of astatine.

parts.question: Predict the physical state of bromine at 20°C. Give a reason for your answer.

parts.label: b(ii)

A long glass tube has cotton wool soaked in concentrated hydrobromic acid at one end and damp blue litmus paper at the other. At first the litmus paper does not turn red, then after a short time it turns red. Explain these observations using the kinetic particle model.

parts.question: Air contains nitrogen, oxygen, noble gases and carbon dioxide. State the percentage of nitrogen in clean, dry air.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: State one adverse effect of oxides of nitrogen on health.

parts.question: Explain why farmers use fertilisers on fields where crops are to be grown.

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.question: Describe a test for potassium ions.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Describe how universal indicator can be used to find the pH of an acidic solution.

parts.question: Choose the pH value that is acidic. Circle your answer.

parts.question: The salt zinc chloride can be prepared by reacting hydrochloric acid with zinc oxide. Choose the type of reaction that occurs. Circle your answer.

parts.question: The method for preparing pure dry crystals of zinc chloride. Steps 1 and 2: Add excess zinc oxide to dilute HCl and warm. Step 4: Evaporate filtrate until point of crystallisation. Step 5: Remove crystals. Complete missing steps 3 and 6.

parts.label: e(i)
parts.question: Small pieces of zinc react with excess dilute HCl at different temperatures. Times recorded: 64s, 16s, 256s for temperatures 20°C, 40°C, 60°C. Complete the table by matching temperatures to times. (Higher temp = faster = shorter time.)

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.question: Describe the effect on the time taken when the reaction is carried out with HCl of a higher concentration. All other conditions stay the same.

parts.question: The structure of compound T is shown (a 4-carbon chain with COOH and OH groups, a hydroxy-acid). Choose the word that describes compound T: alcohol, alkane, alkene, carboxylic acid.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Deduce the formula of compound T to show the number of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms (C₄H₈O₃, a hydroxy-butanoic acid).

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Compound T reacts with ethanol in the presence of a catalyst. State the meaning of the term catalyst.

parts.question: Complete the sentence about ethanol using a word from the list: combustion, cracking, electrolysis, fermentation. Ethanol is manufactured from ethene or by ......................................... .

parts.question: Ethene is a gas at room temperature. Use the kinetic particle model to describe the separation of the particles in a gas.

parts.label: c(iii)

parts.label: c(iv)

parts.question: Name a polymer that is a constituent of food.

parts.question: Chromium is a transition element. Potassium is a Group I element. Chromium has a higher density than potassium. Give two other ways in which the physical properties of chromium differ from potassium.
